title: Drills
summary: Runs of exercises over a lesson's own items, graded by the share answered right.
description: A drill practises a handful of words, sentences or a dialogue. Its cards are built fresh each time: the lesson's level sets the hardest kinds it may use, and each item's familiarity picks among them.

stories.want: each word and sentence to get harder to answer as I get better at it, within what my level is ready for

stories.as: a learner typing on a phone
stories.want: a slip of one letter treated as almost right
stories.soThat: I am graded on my Polish, not my thumbs

stories.as: a beginner in an A1 course
stories.want: cards I can answer with what I know so far
stories.soThat: a drill teaches instead of overwhelming

requirements.text: A word or sentence never answered is shown on a card that is only read, then asked by the easiest kind of card its level allows.

history.text: A word never answered is shown on a card that is only read and then asked by multiple choice; one answered before is asked by multiple choice; one answered right on three different days in a row has to be typed.
history.reason: Card difficulty now follows the lesson's level as well as the learner's history, for sentences as well as words.

requirements.text: Typed answers ignore case, punctuation and spacing, and accept Polish letters typed without their marks.
A typed answer one letter off a word of four letters or more is almost right.
A dictation or spoken sentence of three words or more with one word wrong is almost right.

An almost-right answer is logged as a mistake, earns `drill.almost-share` of the XP, counts as `drill.almost-share` right in the drill's score, and brings the item back sooner instead of starting its reviews over.
A drill passes at `drill.pass-share` right; a drill of three to six scored cards also passes with a single miss, or two almost-right answers.
A drill with `drill.partial-share` or more right that does not pass is a partial; less is a fail.
An ace in a drill is a pass with every scored card fully right.

history.text: An ace in a drill is a pass with no almost-right answers and at least 95% of the scored cards fully right.
history.reason: The owner decided an ace means every answer right: at 95%, a long drill could have a miss and still be an ace.

requirements.text: Cards that are only read (a new word, a dialogue to read, a story panel) are not scored, and a drill with nothing scored is not graded.

On tiles with every form (`tiles-all`) a word that changes its ending is shown in its dictionary form and the learner picks its form from all those stored; on tiles with two (`tiles-two`), from the right one and one other stored form; on tiles with the endings set (`tiles-set`) every word stands as it should. A sentence without stored endings is built by plain ordering.

history.text: A sentence whose words change their ending is built from tiles in dictionary form, and the learner picks the ending on each tile; a sentence without stored endings is built by plain ordering.
history.reason: Picking each ending from every form is too hard for a beginner; easier tile cards come first, by level and familiarity.

requirements.text: A wrong answer on a word shows example sentences for it: made once by a model and kept, or, without a key, taken from the learner's own courses.
After a word or sentence card is answered, the learner can talk about it with the tutor straight from the exercise; that chat has its own model setting and otherwise uses the tutor's model.
Each word's and sentence's review interval grows with right answers on different days, to at most `review.max-interval`; an item counts once a day.

A word's or sentence's card is only of a kind its level allows: `drill.cards-a1` at A1; A2, B1 and B2 add `drill.cards-a2`, `drill.cards-b1` and `drill.cards-b2` in turn, each keeping those below it; C1 and C2 allow every kind.

A known word's or sentence's card is the kind at its familiarity's step in `drill.word-cards` or `drill.sentence-cards`, counting only the kinds its level allows and stopping at the hardest. Familiarity rises by one for each day the item was answered with no miss and falls by one for each day with a miss, never below 0.
The level a drill's cards follow is the lesson's own, else its course's; a lesson and course without one count as A1.
At C1 and C2 a known item starts `drill.c-head-start` steps up its ladder.
Where a card's kind cannot be given (saying aloud with speaking cards off, or beyond a lesson's own cap on them), the next easier kind its level allows is.
A drawing that was not finished when the app closed is resumed the next time it starts, by the device that started it.
A scene or story whose drawing failed says so on its page and can be tried again; a picture lesson offers to draw the pictures still missing.

values.description: The share of a drill answered right that passes it.
The share that is a partial.
What an almost-right answer counts for, of a right answer's score and XP.
The longest a word or sentence waits for its next review.
A word's kinds of card, easiest first: pick its meaning, pick the word, type it from its meaning, write it from hearing it, say it.

A sentence's kinds of card, easiest first: tiles with the endings set, tiles with each ending from two, write it from hearing it with a word bank, tiles with each ending from every form, type its missing word, write it from hearing it, say it.
The kinds of card A1 allows; `gaps-from-bank` fills a few sentences' gaps from a word bank, `pick-picture` links a word and its picture.
How far up its ladder a known item starts at C1 and C2.
